newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel oil talked higher.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel oil talked higher.

text.p: The European straight-run market ended the week on Friday on a positive note, with traders saying it was talked firmer on the back of perceptions of low avails and crude's overnight gains.

No fresh deals were reported, but traders said low sulphur straight-run was talked at $106/$107 early in the day. Later one seller said he offered as high as $110, citing his reason as low prompt avails in the market.
The seller said he cited that figure in response to an inquiry for an 8,000 tonne cargo to load in France, adding than a competitor offered to sell at $2 lower.
But buying interest at those numbers was thin, traders said.
"I am holding back, I want to drive the market up, there is only one seller out there," the seller said.
"There are not that many cargoes left...I expect a deal to be done at $107/$108," he added. Two deals were done earlier this week at $104.50 and $105.50.
Another trader attributed the firmness in straight-run to IPE Brent's higher close on Thursday.
The market, however, was in disagreement about the number of prompt unsold cargoes out there, with some saying about six and other saying only two.
One trader said that there was an offer of Russian straight-run at a low $80 cif Gottenburg.
Traders said that with more Russian straight-run due out in mid-June, it will come off a little.

With a fourth mother-ship docked at St Petersburg this week to tranship barge material and a fifth storage vessel due on station next week, more straight-run should appear on the market, a trader said.

The Norsi refinery at Nizhni Novgorod, east of Moscow, would also pump out more straight-run for export, one trader said, as a result of oil giant Lukoil taking over management of the complex and boosting crude runs.
